title: Functional requirements and quality attributes (non-functional requirements)

videos.script: Two systems can do exactly the same things and need completely different architectures. {{title}} Both sell bus tickets. One handles a hundred sales a day. The other handles two thousand a minute the week before São João, and has to board passengers on a road with no signal. {{same}} What separates them is not the features. It is the qualities. How fast, how available, how secure, how easy to change. {{qualities}} This lesson writes both kinds down so they can be checked. Functional requirements as use cases and acceptance criteria. {{functional}} Quality attributes as scenarios with a number in them. {{scenario}} Then it ranks them in a utility tree, because you cannot make every quality the most important. {{tree}} And it ends by tracing each requirement to the decision that meets it and the test that proves it. {{trace}}
